items.title: Lee Paige Interview, 1961-01-13
items.q: Lee, after you left Ned Waver and the Foundation of Singing and Dancing School

ctx.x: Oh, yes. On the plantation in Kentucky when I was a boy. I was born and raised in a plantation in Kentucky. We had help working around our hired hands. And I used to watch the colored people jump around and dance and sing. And I learned a lot by just watching the hired hands and I'd get ideas from them. And when I was quite a small child, I remember my brother, Richard, he and his buddy came home one day and they wanted me to sing. And I don't, I was so small, I don't remember ever singing. I didn't know what I…
Lee, after you left Ned Waver and the Foundation of Singing and Dancing School, didn't you play at New York at the corporate band and Latin Quarters?

Oh, yes. After taking up the foundation of dancing and everything, the basics of all of it and singing, well then I worked at some of their leading nightclubs there such as the Coke Cabana and the Latin Quarters there, which at that time was two of their most popular nightclubs.
